title: Security & viruses
blurb: Viruses, scam pop-ups, firewall, encryption, safe browsing.

remedies.title: I think my computer has a virus
remedies.why: Unwanted software can arrive from downloads, email attachments and fake updates.

steps.text: If files suddenly have strange extensions or a ransom note appears, unplug the network cable / turn off Wi-Fi and tell IT now.
Run a full scan: Windows Security › Virus & threat protection › Scan options › Full scan (and Microsoft Defender Offline scan for stubborn ones).
Remove programs you don't recognise, sorted by install date.
Remove apps you don't recognise from Applications and Login Items, and check Profiles in Privacy & Security › Profiles (if present).
Change important passwords from a different, clean device.
Keep the system updated; most malware uses old holes.

remedies.escalate: Work computer: stop and tell IT before doing anything else; they may need to look at it as it is.

remedies.title: Pop-up says my computer is infected and to call a number
remedies.why: A website is pretending to be Microsoft or Apple. Real warnings never ask you to call a number.

steps.text: Don't call the number or let anyone connect to your computer.
Close the browser: Ctrl+Shift+Esc › select the browser › End task.
Force Quit the browser: ⌘+Option+Esc.
When you reopen the browser, don't restore the tabs.
If you already called and gave access or paid: disconnect from the internet, tell IT or your bank, and change passwords from another device.

remedies.escalate: If someone remote-connected to the computer, IT must check it before you use it for work or banking.

remedies.title: Windows Security says protection is off
remedies.why: Another antivirus took over, a setting was changed, or (worse) malware switched it off.

steps.text: Open Windows Security and press Turn on for anything red.
If another antivirus is installed, it's the one protecting you; Defender switches off on purpose.
If it won't stay on and you have no other antivirus, run a Defender Offline scan and tell IT.

remedies.title: "Windows protected your PC" stops an app
remedies.why: SmartScreen and Smart App Control block apps Windows hasn't seen much yet; that includes unknown malware and small, honest apps.

steps.text: Only run it if you got it from the maker's own site and expected it.
If you trust it: More info › Run anyway.
Smart App Control can't be bypassed for a single app; look for a signed version or ask the maker.

remedies.escalate: On work PCs, ask IT instead of running blocked apps.

remedies.title: "App can't be opened" or "Apple could not verify"
symptoms: app is damaged and can't be opened
remedies.why: Gatekeeper blocks apps that aren't from the App Store or a verified developer, or that look modified.

steps.text: Only continue for an app from a maker you trust.
Try opening it, then go to Privacy & Security and press Open Anyway near the bottom.
"Damaged": download the app again from the maker's site; don't run copies from unknown sources.

remedies.title: Firewall blocks an app (or asks to allow it)
symptoms: windows defender firewall has blocked some features
remedies.why: The firewall asks before letting an app accept connections from the network.

steps.text: Allow it only for apps you know need it (games, file sharing, remote tools), and only on Private networks.
Change it later: Windows Security › Firewall & network protection › Allow an app through firewall.
System Settings › Network › Firewall › Options lists allowed apps.

remedies.title: Is my disk encrypted? (BitLocker, FileVault)
remedies.why: Encryption keeps your files safe if the laptop is lost or stolen.

steps.text: Settings › Privacy & security › Device encryption (or BitLocker in Control Panel on Pro).
System Settings › Privacy & Security › FileVault.
Before turning it on, save the recovery key somewhere safe outside the computer (your Microsoft/Apple account, or IT).

remedies.title: My laptop was lost or stolen
remedies.why: Act fast: lock or erase it remotely and protect your accounts.

steps.text: Locate or lock it: account.microsoft.com/devices › Find my device (if it was turned on).
Locate, lock or erase it: icloud.com/find or the Find My app on another Apple device.
Change passwords for email and banking, and sign the device out of your accounts.
Report it to the police, and to IT for a work device.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT at once for a work device: they can wipe it and revoke its access.

remedies.title: Review which apps can use my camera, microphone, location and files
remedies.why: Apps ask once and keep access; it's worth checking now and then.

steps.text: Settings › Privacy & security › App permissions (Location, Camera, Microphone…).
System Settings › Privacy & Security, each category lists allowed apps.
